thread:
Raj (Firefly): Hey team, we're seeing a bunch of 429s and 5-7s of extra latency starting 10:10 UTC during a promo spike. Dedicated pool is 'firefly-prod-pool' (4 GPUs). Baseline QPS ~40, peak burst ~820 sustained ~3m, then smoothing to ~300.
Marie (Support): Sorry to hear that — are the 429s auth or rate-limit? Any request ids?
Raj (Firefly): 429s from the inference gateway (x-rw-error=429), not auth. Logs show queue depth on the pool nodes and repeated "overcapacity" in runtime logs. Example log: `2026-02-28T10:10:12Z runtime[pool=firefly-prod] WARN overcapacity request_id=abc123 q=78`.
Josh (SRE): @Raj can you share the pool config? size, autoscale policy, cooldowns? Also are you using prefix caching / KV-warmup?
Raj (Firefly): Pool=4 gpus (A10x4), autoscale min=4 max=12, scale_step=2, cooldown=300s, burst_policy=disabled. No explicit KV-warmup. We relied on default autoscale.
Anya (Solutions Eng): That cooldown is long for sudden marketing bursts. If a single burst pushes to ~800 qps and per-GPU sustained attn throughput ~200 qps, 4 GPUs -> 800 max but that assumes perfect packing and warm KV cache. Startup and cold KV can reduce effective throughput.
Li (Oncall): I'm pulling metrics now — I see CPU/GPU util per node jump to 95% and request queue grow. Autoscaler triggered but respect cooldown and only added 2 GPUs at +3m, which was too late.
Marie (Support): Quick mitigation: enable burst_capacity or temporarily raise max to 16 and lower cooldown; also we can do a short policy to force add +4 immediately. Want us to apply temporary change? :eyes:
Raj (Firefly): Yes please, and we'll also backfill warmup requests. Can you also block noisy tenants? We think another tenant in the same slab had a big ML retrain at same time (noisy neighbor).
Josh (SRE): We'll check tenant isolation. For immediate repro/validation, please run a controlled load:
```
# quick load script (vegeta)
echo "GET http://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate" | vegeta attack -rate=820 -duration=180s | vegeta report
```
That should reproduce the queueing. Also capture `curl -v` response headers to get x-rw-error and request ids.
Anya (Solutions Eng): For capacity planning: if baseline 40 QPS and expected marketing peak 800 QPS, target pool sizing should aim for 60-70% utilization at peak. So target effective capacity = 800 / 0.65 ≈ 1231 QPS, if one GPU delivers ~200 QPS effective (with warm cache) you'd need ~7 GPUs headroom; but because of KV cold starts and variability, plan 10 GPUs reserved + autoscale to 16 for bursts.
Raj (Firefly): Can you run cost vs latency tradeoffs? Customer is budget sensitive.
Anya (Solutions Eng): Yep — rough numbers: A10x throughput cost is X/hour (we'll DM exact). Option A) reserve 8 GPUs — higher baseline cost, latency stable. Option B) keep 4 reserved, add pre-warm script to exercise cache before campaign and set autoscale min=6, max=16, cooldown=60s, scale_step=4. Option B reduces steady cost but risk if autoscale lags.
Josh (SRE): Also tweak request routing: enable per-tenant isolation (noisy tenant blocking) and enable aggressive prefix caching for common prompt templates — reduces per-token work.
Marie (Support): I've applied a temporary override: max=16, cooldown=60s, scale_step=4 on firefly-prod-pool and enabled burst_capacity for 10m. DeployBot: executed policy change (runbook#742).
DeployBot: policy-change applied to pool=firefly-prod-pool by Marie, change_id=chg-20260228-01.
Raj (Firefly): After change we're seeing queue drop and 429s almost gone, latency back to normal within ~90s. Thank you. :thumbsup:
Li (Oncall): Follow-ups: 1) Please run the vegeta script and upload traces; 2) We'll schedule a postmortem with noisy-tenant logs; 3) Recommend weekly warmup jobs before promo windows.
Anya (Solutions Eng): I'll prepare a rightsize recommendation doc with 3 options (cost-first, latency-first, mixed) and run a sims based on your historical qps histogram.
Raj (Firefly): Thanks all — attaching one sample request id abc123 for SRE. We'll coordinate a formal capacity change next week.
Marie (Support): Closing the urgent ticket for now but keeping thread open for the postmortem. :locked_with_key:
